sources: Meehan, Aidan. Celtic Design: Spiral Patterns. London: Thames and Hudson, 1996.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The spiral is a mythic motif. Celtic art is known for its interlocked spirals. The design covers the metalwork of the Celtic lands, from shields to jewelry to tools. The motif lived on into the Christian Middle Ages. The Book of Kells holds a dense spiral ornament. The spiral now reads as Celtic, but the Celts may have taken it. An earlier people, the Megalithic Civilization, carved great spirals on stone. The triple spiral of Newgrange is one such piece. Whether the Celts received the motif from those builders is not yet settled.
